claims.text: The proposed method integrates high-resolution modulated DSC, simultaneous high-temperature dilatometry, and calibrated CALPHAD modeling.
The integrated method can determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties with uncertainty below 10%.
The integrated method significantly outperforms traditional standalone techniques.
The target samples are as-cast, single-phase, well-mixed HEAs, such as an equiatomic Cantor alloy.
Samples will undergo modulated DSC and concurrent dilatometry under an inert atmosphere, with CALPHAD used to benchmark and fit the thermal signals.
Measurements will extend from room temperature to above melting using rapid scan rates and controlled inert-atmosphere conditions.
HEAs intrinsically possess high configurational entropy and atomic-scale disorder.
Configurational entropy and atomic-scale disorder govern HEA phase stability and melting behavior.
Modulated DSC detects detailed heat-flow patterns associated with fusion.
High-temperature dilatometry records the volume change associated with melting.
Integrating DSC and dilatometry with CALPHAD accounts for both thermal and configurational contributions.
The integrated analysis can precisely extract melting parameters and key liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The extracted fusion parameters will consistently be within ±10% of CALPHAD predictions and reference literature values.
Fusion parameters will show systematic compositional dependence consistent with configurational-entropy effects.
Traditional DSC and dilatometry without CALPHAD integration typically have uncertainties greater than 20%.
Traditional standalone methods are less efficient at capturing complex entropic contributions.
The proposed method is most effective for single-phase, well-characterized HEAs.
Accuracy may decrease in multiphase or strongly segregating alloys because overlapping transitions obscure fusion signals.
Calibration challenges and short-range ordering may introduce uncertainty into the DSC-based results.
